root_cause_label: Agent used per-subdirectory setup.py scripts to build Cython extensions in-place, missing the coctree extension and bypassing the canonical top-level build workflow that the evaluator requires
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent built only three of four required Cython extensions using nonstandard subdirectory-level setup.py files rather than the canonical top-level 'python setup.py build_ext --inplace', leaving coctree unbuilt and producing a package state that fails the official acceptance criteria despite the agent's own tests passing.
t_err_evidence: Step 16: agent runs 'cd /app/pyknotid/pyknotid/spacecurves && python setup.py build_ext --inplace' using the pre-existing subdirectory-level setup.py, which only defines the bare 'chelpers' extension, rather than fixing sources and building from the top-level project root via 'python setup.py build_ext --inplace'.
t_commit_evidence: Step 16 locks in the nonstandard approach: the agent subsequently creates additional per-subdirectory setup.py scripts (steps 19, 22) and never revisits the top-level setup.py build route. The fourth extension (coctree in pyknotid/simplify/) is never built.
trigger_explanation: The agent lacked the domain knowledge that the correct workflow for this task is to apply NumPy 2.x compatibility patches to the source files and then invoke 'python setup.py build_ext --inplace' from the project root (which defines all four extensions with fully-qualified module names). Instead, after finding that pip install did not compile extensions, the agent discovered a pre-existing subdirectory setup.py and used it as a template — an ad-hoc approach that omitted the coctree extension entirely and bypassed the official build configuration.
forewarning_evidence: Step 7: pip install produces a 'py3-none-any' wheel (filename=pyknotid-0.5.3-py3-none-any.whl), which signals that no compiled extensions were built. Step 10: same result with editable install — 'pyknotid-0.5.3-0.editable-py3-none-any.whl'. Step 12 and 15: find commands confirm no .so files exist after two pip install attempts.
